claims.text: Introducing nanoscale oxide dispersions into refractory high-entropy alloys will increase their high-temperature yield strength.
Introducing nanoscale oxide dispersions into refractory high-entropy alloys will improve their high-temperature creep resistance.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will improve mechanical performance under irradiation.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will not significantly compromise the thermal stability of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will not significantly compromise the irradiation stability of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering or hot isostatic pressing can produce a refractory HEA containing nanoscale Y2O3 or Al2O3 dispersions.
The predicted benefits should hold at temperatures above 1000 degrees Celsius.
The predicted benefits should hold under neutron or ion irradiation representative of nuclear-reactor conditions.
The intervention will create a uniform dispersion of nanoscale oxide particles within the HEA matrix.
Nanoscale oxide particles impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion improves creep resistance.
Nanoscale oxide particles act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Defect-sink behavior reduces irradiation-induced swelling.
Defect-sink behavior helps maintain microstructural stability during irradiation.
ODS-HEAs will have similar or better resistance to irradiation-induced phase instability than otherwise comparable HEAs without oxide dispersion.
ODS effectiveness depends on oxide-particle size, distribution, and volume fraction.
Effective oxide particles should be smaller than 50 nm.
Excess oxide content or particle agglomeration may reduce ductility or cause embrittlement.
The magnitude of improvement depends on oxide–matrix compatibility and processing.
